programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. TikTok influencer Alexis Sharkey seemed to have the perfect life - she regularly posted videos to her 80,000 followers, but all this came to a sudden end when she disappeared in November 2020. Her parents and friends became increasingly worried and reported her missing - on the 28th of November, 2020, a rubbish truck driver spotted a naked body dumped in the gutter of a side road in Houston. The police confirmed that it was Alexis and revealed that the 26-year-old had been strangled to death - detectives then began a murder investigation and news of the popular influencer's death went viral on TikTok. Just two weeks after Alexis was found dead, her husband Tom also disappeared - however, two of the influencer's closest friends revealed that Alexis had said that she was being abused by him.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels. This undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp now housing asylum seekers. Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences. The film also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town, including a network of surveillance set up by local groups to monitor the camp's residents whenever they leave the site. It also looks at instances of intimidation towards people helping the new arrivals.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

Filming covertly, the programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences.
